newsitem.title: USA: US Senator questions possible Boeing, MD subsidies.
newsitem.headline: US Senator questions possible Boeing, MD subsidies.

text.p: U.S. Senator Tom Harkin wrote Defense Secretary William Cohen on Tuesday asking if taxpayer money will be used to subsidise the proposed merger of Boeing Co and McDonnell Douglas Corp.

"I would respectfully request that the Department of Defense determine whether or not taxpayer dollars will be used to subsidize the Boeing/McDonnell Douglas merger, and, if so, I would appreciate an estimate of how much this subsidy will cost the taxpayer," the Iowa Democrat wrote.
A Pentagon spokeswoman declined to comment. "We have not seen the letter," she said.
A spokesman for Harkin said that by law defense companies that merge can apply for subsidies known as "allowable costs," which are made as part of Pentagon procurement payments.

But Pengaton officials have said that any time a company restructures to save money for taxpayers it will compensate up to half those savings, as provided by law. If mergers save money, then they qualify.
The reimbursements exclude such direct costs of merging as lawyers fees or buy-outs for executives.

Harkin wrote that he had "serious concerns about whether the federal government should share in the merger costs for an arrangement whose very announcement resulted in huge increases in the value of both companies' stock."
